thesis: Solarvest shows improving project profitability but has not delivered per-share growth: Q1 EPS fell to 1.99 sen from 2.11 despite higher profit. The bear carries that distinction at 48x trailing earnings, with expansion outlays exceeding the dated simple FCF bridge. A verified RM2.371bn backlog and margin improvement preserve future conversion upside, while March funding data cannot stand in for June liquidity.
strongest_counterexample: Q1 revenue grew 13.2%, margin improved to 12.2% from 11.5%, and FY26 CFO turned positive; profitable project delivery could eventually outgrow dilution.
invalidation_conditions: A comparable Q1 basic EPS above the prior 2.11 sen with margin at least the observed 12.2% would weaken the current per-share-growth objection.
Verified current statements showing positive cash after PP&E, intangibles, investment-property and associate/JV outlays would weaken the external-expansion-funding objection.
evidence_gaps: Latest June 30 full balance-sheet/cash-flow attachment was inaccessible; available March figures are explicitly older.
decisive_factors: Current profit growth and falling EPS are disclosed facts read differently, not a valuation-model gap.
FY26 RM386.821m equity-related funding and capital-intensive growth offset the positive orderbook.
